title: Embedded Fidelity Experiments — Launch Guide & Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This playbook describes the strategy, success criteria, rollout plan, telemetry, and operational controls for the Embedded Fidelity Experiments feature. The feature enables customers to opt into lower-cost, lower-fidelity model execution modes for the Embedded/Edge runtime (on-device or lightweight cloud instances) so teams can measure economics and quality trade-offs in production-like conditions.

Audience
- Product managers (Fidelity & Embedded)
- Partner engineering and solutions teams
- Applied ML (onboarding & evals)
- DevEx and Docs for developer-facing flows
- SRE and Observability for telemetry and alerts

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Provide a controlled experiment surface for customers to test quantized or reduced-fidelity variants in embedded deployments.
  - Measure end-to-end cost savings (target: 20–35% token cost reduction) while bounding quality regression (target: <1.5% drop on business eval metrics).
  - Surface per-route fidelity analytics in Console and Optimize advisor.
- Non-goals:
  - Automatic descheduling of high-fidelity traffic across Dedicated GPUs (handled by existing routing policies).
  - Replacing full model-marketplace skus; this is an experimentation & onboarding path.

Key definitions
- Fidelity Variant: a runtime-compatible model variant (quantized/size-reduced) with a defined fidelity tag (e.g., fidelity:lo-8bit-v1).
- Embedded Runtime: the lightweight runtime used for on-device or edge-hosted inference (binary: redwood-embedd).
- Experiment Unit: a per-tenant per-route toggle that samples X% of requests to a fidelity variant.

Success criteria (initial pilot)
1) Telemetry: end-to-end telemetry available in Console for pilot customers (latency, cost per token, regression_rate).
2) Economics: median cost-per-token reduction >= 20% for pilot routes without increased infra incidents.
3) Quality: business eval set degradation <= 1.5% for each participating tenant OR failed rollouts auto-reverted.
4) Developer UX: partner onboarding checklist completed in < 3 business days for 80% of partners.

Safety & guardrails
- Hard limits: max experiment sample per route = 30% (configurable by support).
- Auto-rollback: if telemetry.metric.fidelity.regression_rate > 3.0% or latency.p90 increases > 40% vs baseline for 30 minutes, experiments are automatically disabled for that route and an incident is filed.
- Confidentiality: experiments are internal-only by default; no customer data leaves the private runtime unless explicit consent documented in contract addendum.

Rollout phases and timeline
1) Internal lab (2 weeks) — engineering + applied ML
   - Run simulated traffic using the consumption-simulator and PRD test vectors.
   - Verify metrics: latency.p50/p90, cost delta, eval-set F1/BLEU/Embedding-sim.
   - Owners: eng-serving-runtime (lead: Priya Nair), applied-ml (lead: Carlos Kim).
2) Partner beta (6 weeks) — 3 strategic customers across edge and cloud-embedded use cases
   - Onboard partners using the partner-onboarding checklist (see Related Pages).
   - Enable experiment units at 5% -> 15% -> 30% staged cadence over 2-week windows.
   - Biweekly check-ins; run regression tests after each stage.
   - Owners: product (Maya Chen), customer-success (lead: Hannah Lee).
3) Public opt-in (GA candidate)
   - Expose toggle in Console under Runtime > Experiments > Embedded Fidelity.
   - Default sample = 0% (opt-in).
   - Provide SDK flags and CLI: redwood-embedd --experiment fidelity:lo-8bit-v1 --sample 0.05

Detailed rollout checklist (Partner beta)
1. Pre-onboard
   - Verify contract/consent: legal addendum signed (if private data).
   - Allocate telemetry retention: 14 days event retention for pilot (observability-config: fidelity-experiments-14d).
2. Onboarding (day 0–2)
   - Configure partner route(s) with Experiment Unit (UI/CLI).
   - Baseline collection: 72h baseline traffic capture.
3. Stage 1 (5%) — 7 days
   - Validate no increase in infra errors (5xx) and stable resource utilization.
   - Run shadow-eval: capture outputs from both variants for offline evaluation.
4. Stage 2 (15%) — 7 days
   - Check business metrics and run end-to-end user-flow smoke tests.
5. Stage 3 (30%) — 7 days
   - Final gating decision: accept, pause, or rollback.

Telemetry & observability (what to collect)
- Core metrics (per-tenant, per-route, tagged by variant):
  - latency.p50, latency.p90 (ms)
  - cost.per_token.usd (simulated and realized)
  - fidelity.regression_rate (business eval metric drop percentage)
  - error_rate.5xx, server_errors
  - kvcache.hit_rate (where applicable)
- Traces & logs:
  - Add structured logs: experiment.variant, experiment.sample_rate, baseline.request_id
  - Tracing: annotate spans with fidelity.variant and fidelity.switch_time
- Console dashboard: Fidelity Experiments -> Overview, Route-level breakdown, Regression heatmap (7d/30d)

APIs and config examples
- CLI example (embed runtime):
  - redwood-embedd config set-experiment --route invoices-create --variant fidelity:lo-8bit-v1 --sample 0.05
- JSON API payload example:
  - { "route": "invoices-create", "experiment": { "variant": "fidelity:lo-8bit-v1", "sample": 0.15, "start_ts": "2026-11-05T00:00:00Z" } }

Developer experience (Docs & SDKs)
- DevEx deliverables before public opt-in:
  - Quickstart: embedded-fidelity-quickstart.md (includes CLI and SDK snippets).
  - Example repo: github.com/redwood/embed-fidelity-examples (conversational, summarization, retrieval).
  - Playground: sandbox widgets to run side-by-side comparisons with token accounting.

Evaluation methodology and metrics
- Offline shadow-eval pipeline: collect outputs for N requests in parallel from both variants and compute: embedding_cosine_mean, rouge_l, domain-specific scoring.
- Business metric anchoring: each partner must provide a 5–10 item business eval set (mandatory) for guardrail scoring.
- Threshold policy: if any metric drop > 1.5% AND embedding_cosine_mean delta > 0.02, mark as degraded and require human review.

Operational runbook (high-level)
1) Alert: fidelity.regression_rate_alert firing -> oncall SRE (pager)
2) Immediate actions:
   - Reduce experiment sample to 0% via emergency API and tag incident: EX-FIDELITY-<route>-<ts>
   - Capture last 24h shadow-eval artifacts to /s3/pilot-artifacts/<tenant>/<route>/
   - Notify product and partner success; schedule postmortem within 48h if incident linked to fidelity experiment.
3) Recovery and learnings:
   - If automated rollback resolved the issue, create a retrospective and update variant scoring table and rollout gating rules.

Ownership and escalation
- Product (Maya Chen) — product decisioning and partner coordination
- Applied ML (Carlos Kim) — variant selection, eval pipeline, quality thresholds
- Eng-Serving-Runtime (Priya Nair) — runtime flags, kernel selection, perf tuning
- Observability (Lena Ortiz) — dashboards, alerts, telemetry schema
- Customer Success (Hannah Lee) — partner onboarding and comms

Known limitations and future work
- Current runtimes supported: redwood-embedd v1.x only. Support for v2 and hardware-accelerated edge (NPU) planned Q2 2027.
- Automatic fidelity negotiation (runtime-driven decisioning) is out of scope for initial release — future product iteration.
- Telemetry volume increases: expect +10–20% event volume during pilot; budget with Observability team.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Experiment telemetry schema (key -> description)
  - fidelity.variant_id -> canonical variant name
  - fidelity.sample_rate -> fraction sent to variant
  - fidelity.regression_rate -> percent drop on partner eval set
- Appendix B: Partner checklist (one-page)
  - Signed addendum? [Y/N]
  - Baseline capture completed? [Y/N]
  - SDK/CLI test passed? [Y/N]
  - Telemetry dashboard shared? [Y/N]

References
- See Related Pages and Console > Runtime > Experiments for links to onboarding docs, sandbox designs, and the offline eval harness.

Change log
